findings.title: M auxiliary scoring is connected to the first deployed11 projected directions
findings.finding: The active training wrapper stores the first modality_projection output as F.normalize(output.float(), dim=-1), requires shape [B,7,512] and requires_grad, and never detaches it. The second M pool calls the existing pool_score on this cached tensor, then returns Z * weights[...,None] * 7. The caller takes mean(1), and the neck pre-hook verifies the exact pooled feature. Clearing the Python frame after forward does not itself detach the returned tensor's autograd graph.
findings.conclusion: No source-supported detach, missing first11 selection, frozen M scorer, or substitution of raw/controlled M evidence was found. Source connectivity does not prove a nonzero numerical gradient.

findings.title: The live nonzero-loss M scorer route is the auxiliary route
findings.finding: Main11 is produced by the expert reads, conditions, router and fuse, without calling modality_expert.pool_score. The first independent M pool contributes controlled10, but same_state_targets is under no_grad and does not propagate the contribution regression back through those target states. The later second M pool supplies the auxiliary identity feature. Partial=True returns before auxiliary pools; the partial loss weights are zero.
findings.conclusion: A positive main loss or positive PM projection gradient cannot certify that this M scoring parameter receives a nonzero update gradient. Its trainable state and use in the graph remain intentional; removing it or changing the gate is not a supported repair.

findings.title: X repairs the F scorer only; M's second scorer remains inside CUDA autocast
findings.finding: AC delegates construction/update to X. X installs its FP32 wrapper only on frequency_expert.pool_score, and only for its actual 3D auxiliary input. M's cached normalized input is FP32, but M's linear scoring call has no local autocast-disabled region and is executed inside the outer training autocast context. A FP32 input tensor alone is not a promise of FP32 linear arithmetic. Current run metadata records torch 2.5.1+cu121/native fp16 GradScaler512, and the saved axis trace confirms only F's 3D scorer output is FP32.
findings.conclusion: The remaining M scoring precision is a concrete observation target. This source review does not report an observed ordinary M output dtype or identify a unique rounding/underflow/cancellation operation.

findings.title: Ordinary relation slots share evidence, but are not algebraically forced identical
findings.finding: frequency_shared maps to the ordinary-frequency variant. Its ModalityAxisExpert.read uses values[:, :, band] for every relation, whereas structured axis uses values[:, subset, band]. Both still have relation-specific query parameters and routed conditioning. Thus the ordinary seven M directions can be much closer, but exact equality is not imposed by the source.
findings.hypothesis: Small within-sample variation among the seven normalized PM directions can make the scorer VJP very small or cancellation-sensitive; changed hard-batch membership/upstream mining may expose that at the current .001 auxiliary weight.
not_established: Loss of sensitivity in a particular FP16 operation
The cause of the current final predicate failure
Any retrieval benefit from changing precision

findings.title: Weighted auxiliary scaling and the native gate must retain their current semantics
findings.finding: The M auxiliary loss is .001 times the inherited .25*CE + 1*softTriplet. At configured scale512 these coefficients multiply the scaled loss by .128 and .512 respectively; they do not determine any parameter-gradient magnitude. optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) runs at the start of every attempt. Full and zero-weight partial backwards are followed by unscale/step/update. The final all-parameter predicate inspects the retained gradients of the last attempt at which three successful updates have been reached, not a union over all attempts.
findings.conclusion: Neither raw unscaled diagnostic autograd calls nor a nonzero value at an earlier attempt substitutes for the native scaled-full-backward/last-attempt predicate. Keep the gate unchanged; do not add artificial losses, increase weights, count any historical nonzero, or interpret an Adam/weight-decay parameter delta as proof of nonzero loss gradient.

findings.title: The sampler factor changes the observed seed42 native batches without a source change to the optimizer
findings.finding: The saved CPU report covers 50 formal-epoch schedules/6563 batches with P8K8, exact record multisets and post-sampler RNG equality. It is not a saved ordinary native trace. The actual AC axis native records seed42, 130 generated epoch batches, 75 swaps, post-sampler RNG equality and three successful updates. Read-only comparison with the two saved X native traces shows one K8 group differs in each of the first three batches; X ordinary/axis names themselves match. Partial sets remain R, N, T.

The ordinary gate location implies these per-call assertions did not abort. However, ordinary actual names/attempt count/tensor values were not saved; axis details cannot be relabeled as ordinary measurements. Different groups and upstream gradients prevent treating historical X success as proof of the current M numerical cause.

findings.title: The previous W F diagnosis motivates a test, not a transferred diagnosis
findings.finding: The saved W F readout reports native scorer weight nnz 0/3/0 and same-Z/weight/scaled-full-incoming FP32 local VJP nnz 512/512/512. Current AC has no corresponding M observation. W's F pooled expression uses sum(1); current M explicitly multiplies by7 and then mean(1).

mathematical_interpretation.definition: Ignoring finite-precision roundoff only, q=sum_s a_s*z_s, a=softmax(Z*w). For incoming h, dL/dw=sum_s a_s * <h,z_s-q> * z_s.
mathematical_interpretation.implication: Exactly equal relation vectors make the real-arithmetic scorer derivative zero; small spread can make it weak through the centered term. The source's ordinary shared-value reading makes this a plausible measurement target but does not establish equality or an actual zero derivative.
mathematical_interpretation.diagnostic_arithmetic_constraint: The local M replay must use the actual `(Z * softmax(linear(Z,w))[...,None] * 7).mean(1)` operation order. It must not replace this by F's `.sum(1)` on the grounds of real-arithmetic equivalence.
